regions.label: MZ header
regions.note: DOS EXE header, rebuilt by the museum unpacker after removing the DIET compression.

regions.label: Relocation table
regions.note: 1 segment addresses that DOS patches with the real load address.

regions.label: Header padding
regions.note: Fills the header to a 16-byte boundary.

regions.label: Main: 16 calls
regions.note: Mode 12h, then 16 copies of “set DX, AX, CX, BX, call 0284”, then back to DOS with the picture still on screen.

regions.label: 16 strings
regions.note: fsl hggi hgvplk hgvpdl (the Basmala on an Arabic keyboard), each with its own style keys in front.

regions.label: Engine entry
regions.note: Saves the ARABART-style registers and translates each key into a glyph code, in place.

regions.label: Shaper
regions.note: 136 bytes identical to ARABART 4.15: two neighbors stay joined only if both join bits allow it.

regions.label: Glyph drawing
regions.note: Styles, glyph runs and VGA graphics controller writes.

regions.label: Engine variables
regions.note: Text address, x, y, color and style flags.

regions.label: His name and Al-Nour
regions.note: ياسر محمد علي, his name, and مركز النور للكومبيوتر, Al-Nour Computer Center, typed as keyboard keys with his style markup.

regions.label: Row address table
regions.note: 500 entries, 80 bytes apart: the start of each VGA row.

regions.label: VGA tables
regions.note: Segment A000h, the bit-reverse table 0 4 2 6 1 5 3 7, and pixel masks 80h to 01h.

regions.label: Key to glyph table
regions.note: 96 entries for ASCII 20h-7Fh; the top two bits of each code are the join bits.

regions.label: Font
regions.note: Glyph pointer table and glyph runs. 2,758 of these bytes are identical to ARABART 4.15.

routines.name: arabart_entry
routines.note: The same registers as the ARABART TSR, reached with CALL instead of INT 10h.

lines.note: Key to glyph code through the table at 09FB

routines.name: sixteen_calls
routines.note: Every mix of bold, underline and italic, at two sizes.

lines.note: Call 9: *$ resets and doubles the size
